findings.title: Lithuanian login TOTP step text replaced with Italian
findings.body: The `loginTotpStep1` value was changed from a Lithuanian sentence to the Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will now see Italian text on the OTP setup page. A Lithuanian translation, or removing the key so it falls back to English, would be correct.

findings.title: Lithuanian account TOTP step text replaced with Italian
findings.body: `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account bundle now reads 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. The user-facing page will show the wrong language. The same copy-paste mistake appears in the Lithuanian login bundle.

findings.title: zh_CN account TOTP step replaced with Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: `totpStep1` in the Simplified Chinese bundle now contains Traditional Chinese ('在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：'). It was copied from zh_TW. Simplified-Chinese users get mismatched script, and the same file uses Simplified Chinese elsewhere.

findings.title: English-file path derivation is fragile and only covers some layouts
findings.body: The regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` is greedy. It is not anchored to the file name and can match earlier in the path. The mapping `resources-community` to `resources` works for the themes module, but account-ui and admin-ui keep the community files in `maven-resources-community`. That path is rewritten to `maven-resources`, which only works by accident. If the English file is missing, the verifier throws a RuntimeException instead of reporting a message, which makes the build crash on any file whose English counterpart is not found.

findings.title: HTML detection regex misses uppercase and slash-prefixed tags
findings.body:
`HTML_TAGS` is `<[a-z]+[^>]*>`. It is case-sensitive, so an English value containing `` or `
` would not count as HTML. It also matches non-HTML such as `` placeholders, which would wrongly enable the permissive policy for a translation. The 'English has HTML' gate is therefore both over- and under-inclusive.

findings.title: Anchor tag comparison is order-based and removes only the first textual match
findings.body: `santizeAnchors` pairs the Nth anchor tag in the translation with the Nth in the English text. A reordered but otherwise identical set of anchors is reported as invalid. `value.replaceFirst(...)` removes the first occurrence of the string regardless of position, while the matcher keeps iterating over the original `value`. Both can misbehave when the same anchor tag appears several times. The `key` parameter is also unused.

findings.title: Tests only assert that an error appears, not the positive case
findings.body: The new tests use only `hasItem(containsString(...))`. No test verifies that a valid file, or one with legitimate HTML such as `<strong>` or allowed anchors, produces no messages. `noHtml_en.properties` is added but never used as a clean case. The duplicate-keys assertion was also weakened from `contains` to `hasItem`. False positives in the new verifier would go undetected.

findings.title: New dependencies not added to the plugin's managed/compile classpath consistently
findings.body: `owasp-java-html-sanitizer` is added without an explicit scope and `commons-text` with `compile`. Versions are hard-coded rather than taken from the parent's dependency management. The plugin is built standalone, but this risks version drift and pulls in transitive dependencies (guava, commons-lang3) that are not reviewed.
